target_customer: Health app developers and startups that must store protected health information; later ecommerce businesses needing consumer privacy compliance
problem: Developers of health apps had to build HIPAA technical safeguards themselves or rent expensive compliant hosting. TrueVault offered a compliant data store and API with a signed business associate agreement. It later moved to privacy law compliance software for ecommerce.
product_category: HIPAA compliant data API, later privacy compliance software

founders.name: Jason Wang
founders.background_notes: Background from the YC company page; the TrueVault about page lists him as Founder and CEO.

founders.name: Trey Swann
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article of 2014-02-14; the YC page lists only Jason Wang. No background found.

competitors.name: Amazon Web Services
competitors.what: HIPAA eligible hosting on dedicated instances with a business associate agreement
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; article says dedicated instances start near 1,500 dollars a month

competitors.name: FireHost
competitors.traction_then: Not stated; article says plans start near 1,115 dollars a month

technical_complexity.rationale: Encrypted yet searchable storage with audit logging and an API that a small team had to harden to HIPAA standards, but built on standard cloud infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance work and stored data create some lock in, but hosts such as AWS already offered business associate agreements and the API layer could be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hosting providers kept offering compliant infrastructure; no source found of an incumbent copying or buying TrueVault. The company later changed focus to ecommerce privacy compliance.

market_need_then: HIPAA compliance was costly for early digital health apps; the launch article cites about 200 customers within days of launch and the seed coverage reports roughly 300 clients.

branding.domain_note: Uses truevault.com; an earlier safe.truevault.com subdomain hosted the HIPAA product pages. How the domain was acquired is not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, compliance focused; company pages stress simple, automated privacy compliance.

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows press about the brand itself, merch or community. The name signals security but is generic and shares words with unrelated companies in trademark records.

pivots.from: HIPAA compliant data storage API for health apps
pivots.to: consumer data privacy compliance software for ecommerce
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; inferred only from the current homepage versus the 2014 launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: TrueVault launched out of YC in early 2014 with a HIPAA data API, drew about 200 customers within days and closed a 2.5 million dollar seed on demo day. It is still operating, now selling privacy compliance software to ecommerce brands, which suggests the original health API market was too narrow or too contested by cloud hosts. No exit or shutdown found.
notes: Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Investors for the seed came from a search summary of TechCrunch coverage and VCPost; one summary lists an LLC including Andreessen, not recorded. CB Insights and Parsers list a 3.72M Series A on 2018-09-10 and about 6.24M total, seen only on aggregators, so unverified and not recorded as a round. A later report cites 3.2M raised from outside investors. Per-API-call price conflicts between outlets (0.001 vs 0.01 dollars). Current CEO on about page is Jason Wang; a search snippet naming Jillian Straw as CEO conflicts with the about page, which lists her as Head of Customer Growth.
